sector_model: large-cap biopharma: product revenue concentration, FCF after SBC, net cash after acquisition financing, pipeline and acquired intangibles
thesis: Vertex Pharmaceuticals (Nasdaq: VRTX), cystic fibrosis franchise plus Journavx, Casgevy and, since 2026-09-01, Crinetics (Palsonify, atumelnant). Q3 2026 (10-Q filed 2026-11-03): revenue 3,440.8M (+11.8% vs 3,076.4M), operating income 712.9M (vs 1,186.2M), net income 653.6M (diluted EPS 2.56 vs 4.20). The profit drop reflects the Crinetics deal: 409.6M accelerated equity award expense and 58.9M transaction costs in SG&A, SG&A 844.1M vs 445.1M, R&D 1,320.6M vs 977.7M. Crinetics cost 10.0B cash equity value (9.0B net of acquired cash); goodwill 1,335.4M, Palsonify intangible 3,010.0M, atumelnant IPR&D 5,116.0M. Financing: 4,496.8M term loan proceeds in 9M; debt 999.6M short-term plus 3,497.0M long-term (about 4.50B) vs zero at 2025-12-31. Cash and marketable securities 9,821.2M (vs 12,320.4M at year end), so net cash about 5.32B. 9M OCF 3,196.6M less capex 342.9M = FCF 2,853.7M; TTM OCF 3,694.6M (FY25 3,631.4 - 9M25 3,133.4 + 3,196.6) less TTM capex 492.3M = FCF 3,202.3M. At 538.60 (2026-11-13 close, 52-week 412.27-568.67) and 253.54M shares, market cap about 136.6B, EV about 131.2B, TTM FCF yield 2.3%, EV/FCF 41x; TTM SBC about 668.6M (includes the 409.6M one-off acceleration), FCF after SBC about 2.53B (1.9%). Trailing GAAP P/E about 34.6x (stockanalysis) is depressed by acquisition charges, so ex-charge multiples are lower but I did not reconcile them. Buybacks 933.1M in 9M but only 120.8M in Q3 as cash went to the deal. Why the market may price it this way: a 34x trailing multiple on 12% growth assumes Journavx and Casgevy ramps plus pipeline value; what differs: the CF franchise is highly cash generative and net cash remains large; what would close the gap: product revenue splits and guidance, which I did not read.
counterthesis: Quality is high but price attractiveness is not shown: FCF yield about 2.3% with 12% growth. Cystic fibrosis revenue is concentrated, with competition and patent timelines I did not review. The 10B Crinetics deal paid for pre-revenue IPR&D (5.1B atumelnant) that can be written down on trial failure, and leverage went from zero to 4.5B (term loan terms, rates and covenants unread). Opioid-alternative Journavx and Casgevy ramps are unverified. Product revenue breakdown, guidance and legal proceedings were in truncated parts of the 10-Q and the earnings release (8-K 2026-11-02, URL not retrievable) was not read. Form 144 filings 11-06 and 11-12 indicate insider sales (content unread).
invalidation: Thesis would fail if CF revenue growth stalls, Journavx or Casgevy ramps disappoint, atumelnant trials fail forcing impairment, or the term loan and integration costs constrain buybacks and returns.
